holidays.name: International Picnic Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to grabbing a blanket, a basket of snacks, and eating outdoors with ants as uninvited guests. Parks worldwide fill up with people munching sandwiches on the grass.
holidays.origin: An unofficial observance that grew out of the long tradition of outdoor dining, which became fashionable in Victorian England and across Europe in the 19th century. Its exact founder is unclear and it spread mostly through social media and food-loving communities.
holidays.funFact: The word 'picnic' likely comes from the 17th-century French 'piquenique,' and early picnics were actually indoor potluck-style gatherings where each guest brought something to share.

holidays.name: Autistic Pride Day
holidays.description: A celebration of the autistic community that emphasizes neurodiversity, acceptance, and pride rather than cure narratives. People often wear rainbow infinity symbols and share personal stories.
holidays.origin: Launched in 2005 by the group Aspies For Freedom, which wanted autistic people to celebrate their identities and challenge stigma. It is held on June 18 each year and is now observed worldwide.
holidays.funFact: The rainbow infinity symbol is commonly used for the day because it represents the infinite variety and diversity of the autism spectrum.

holidays.name: Go Fishing Day
holidays.description: A day when you are encouraged to drop everything, grab a rod, and head to the nearest lake, river, or pier. Catching a fish is optional, but sitting around telling tall tales about the one that got away is basically mandatory.
holidays.origin: An unofficial observance in the United States that takes place around the start of summer, when fishing season is in full swing. It was created to encourage people to get outdoors and enjoy the sport and relaxation of angling.
holidays.funFact: Fishing is one of the most popular outdoor activities in the United States, with tens of millions of people casting a line each year.

holidays.name: Sushi Day
holidays.description: A day to roll up your sleeves, or at least order delivery, and honor the art of vinegared rice topped with fish, veggies, and whatever else the chef feels like wrapping in seaweed.
holidays.origin: This food observance was created by sushi fans and restaurants to celebrate Japan's famous culinary export, which began as a method of preserving fish in fermented rice centuries ago.
holidays.funFact: The wasabi served at many sushi restaurants outside Japan is actually horseradish dyed green, since real wasabi is expensive and hard to grow.

holidays.name: International Panic Day
holidays.description: A tongue-in-cheek day on which you are officially allowed to freak out about everything, from missed deadlines to the dishes in the sink. Think of it as a permission slip to run in circles and flail your arms.
holidays.origin: An unofficial and humorous observance that appeared on quirky holiday calendars as a playful counterpoint to all the calm, mindful days on the calendar. It has no known founder and is celebrated mostly for laughs.
holidays.funFact: The word 'panic' comes from the Greek god Pan, whose sudden shouts in the wilderness were said to cause terror in travelers and livestock.
